name: Sunset Boulevard to the Pacific
blurb: Sunset Boulevard, all the way from downtown to the ocean.

texts: Sunset Boulevard gave its name to a famous film, from 1950.
Los Angeles will host the Summer Olympics again in 2028, its third time.
Echo Park Lake began as a drinking-water reservoir in the 1860s.
Echo Park Lake is famous for its lotus flowers, celebrated each summer with a festival.
The first film studio in Hollywood opened a few blocks from here, on Sunset, in 1911.
The Hollywood sign went up in 1923. It first read Hollywoodland, to sell new houses on the hill.
Hollywood joined the city of Los Angeles in 1910, largely for its water.
For Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, in 2019, whole stretches of Sunset and Hollywood Boulevard were dressed back to how they looked in 1969.
The Sunset Strip is about a mile and a half long, and for decades sat just outside the Los Angeles city limits.
Clubs on the Strip, like the Whisky a Go Go, helped launch some of the biggest bands of the sixties.
The Beverly Hills Hotel opened in 1912, before there was a city of Beverly Hills.
The Beverly Hills Hotel is known as the Pink Palace, for its famous pink walls.
Sunset Boulevard ends right by the ocean, where it meets the Pacific Coast Highway.
The Santa Monica Mountains here are part of the Transverse Ranges, among the few mountain ranges in America that run east to west.
The coast just south of here, around Santa Monica and Venice, is known as Silicon Beach, for all its tech companies.
